title: Nvidia Expands Amkor AI Packaging Deal to $3B
summary:
Tesla and Nvidia will invest $2.8B in a Samsung Electro-Mechanics plant to establish dedicated production lines in Sejong and Busan, according to Korean media. Nvidia also expanded its agreement with Amkor Technology to $3B to secure AI packaging capacity, a move that pushed Amkor shares 8.4% higher in premarket trading. Samsung Electro-Mechanics additionally signed the largest substrate contract in its company history with Nvidia for chips and networking switches.

These investments build on GTC Berlin commitments to address supply chain constraints through a more than 300% increase in Amkor's advanced packaging capacity by 2028 and a 15x boost in SPIL's optical-engine manufacturing by mid-2027. Other agreements with IBIDEN and Unimicron aim to lift substrate capacity 2.5x over three years, and a $1.1B advance will fund new KYEC testing facilities in the U.S. by April 2027. CEO Jensen Huang stated that capacity is the primary constraint as demand for AI infrastructure remains extraordinary.

selectedTweets.text:
NVIDIA & AMKOR $AMKR PLAN OVER 300% EXPANSION IN ADVANCED PACKAGING CAPACITY

NVIDIA announced new agreements with major semiconductor supply chain partners at GTC Berlin to expand manufacturing capacity for its current and next-generation AI platforms.

Here's what's planned:

• Amkor: Increase advanced packaging interposer wafer capacity in South Korea by more than 300% by the end of 2028, alongside new manufacturing facilities.

• IBIDEN, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, and Unimicron: Expand substrate capacity by 2.5x over the next three years, with production expansions across Japan, South Korea, and Taiwan.

• KYEC: Build new semiconductor testing facilities in the U.S., supported by a $1.1 billion capacity reservation advance from NVIDIA. High-volume production is targeted for April 2027.

• SPIL: Increase optical-engine manufacturing capacity for co-packaged optics by 15x by mid-2027, with plans to double it again by the end of 2028.

• Semiconductor Testing: NVIDIA expects its overall testing capacity to double from 2026 to 2027, supported by expansions in the U.S., Taiwan, and Singapore.

Jensen Huang said:

“We are in the midst of the largest infrastructure buildout in human history. Demand is extraordinary. Capacity is the constraint.”

The expansion is intended to increase production capacity and strengthen NVIDIA's global supply chain as demand for AI infrastructure continues to grow.

selectedTweets.text:
According to Korean media, Samsung Electro Mechanics just signed the biggest substrate contract in its history, and the customer is $NVDA.

The multibillion dollar deal covers the substrates that sit under Nvidia's AI chips and networking switches, with new dedicated lines in Sejong and Busan.

At GTC Berlin, Nvidia said deals with Samsung Electro Mechanics, IBIDEN and Unimicron will lift its substrate capacity 2.5X over the next three years.

$AMKR plans to grow interposer capacity in Korea by more than 300% by the end of 2028, and Nvidia is giving KYEC a $1.1 billion advance to build new test facilities in the United States.

Nvidia is now paying suppliers up front just to make sure the capacity exists.

You do not prepay for capacity you think you will not need, this is Nvidia telling us demand is still running AHEAD of supply.
selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
The memory shortage is now spreading to the parts UNDERNEATH the chips.

According to Korean media, Samsung Electro Mechanics just signed a 360.5 billion won supply contract, about $267 million, for package substrates used in memory semiconductors.The customer is a large global company that was not named and the deal covers all of 2027.

What makes this interesting is that it is the company's FIRST long term supply agreement for package substrates because until now its long term deals were for components like capacitors and inductors.

It is also the seventh long term agreement Samsung Electro Mechanics has announced this year, bringing the total to roughly 4.3 trillion won.

Customers do not lock in supply a full year ahead unless they are worried about not getting enough of it.

I think this is another sign the AI buildout is creating bottlenecks across the ENTIRE supply chain, not just in HBM and DRAM.
